newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's petroleum output seen up 11.1 pct in '97.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's petroleum output seen up 11.1 pct in '97.

text.p: Brazil's petroleum output is expected to rise 11.1 percent to one million barrels a day in 1997 from the current 900,000 barrels, a Petrobras top official said.
Petroleum output is forecast to reach 1.2 million barrels a day in 1998, and rise to 1.5 million barrels daily in 2000, said Petrobras president Joel Renno.
Brazil imports this year would be around $500 million a month, he added.

Currently, Brazil imports half of the total petroleum it uses, but as domestic production is expected to rise in the next years the share of imports is likely to drop to around 30 percent at the end of the decade, Renno said.
